title: Research an Account Before a Meeting (Search, Scrape, Brief)
summary: How go-to-market teams and their coding agents research one company before a call with Cargo: a Google search, a scrape of the company's own pages, a news search and its open roles, each line of the briefing traceable to a source. Commands, prices and returned fields.
body_markdown:
**To research an account before a go-to-market meeting, run four Cargo actions on the company’s domain: a Google search (` serper.search` ), a scrape of its own pages (` firecrawl.scrape` ), a dated news search (` exa.search` ) and a search of its open roles (` theirStack.searchJobs` ). Then write a one-page briefing where every line names the source it came from.**


This is the one-off research job: one company, one meeting, run from a terminal or by a coding agent. It is the[research-account](https://www.getcargo.ai/skills/research-account) skill. If you want a briefing posted to Slack every time an external meeting is booked, that is the deployed[meeting-prep cookbook](https://www.getcargo.ai/cookbooks/meeting-prep) instead.


## The data behind it#


Cargo platform data, 90 days to Oct 16 2026: about 435k Google searches through Serper and 296k page scrapes through Firecrawl ran on Cargo. Search and scrape are the two most used research steps on the platform, and both cost 0.05 credits a call.


## Run it#


### 1. Install and sign in


shellscript


```text
npm   install   -g   @cargo-ai/cli
cargo-ai   login   --email   you@company.com                   # sends a code
cargo-ai   login   --email   you@company.com   --code   123456     # creates the account on first use


```


There is no browser step, so a coding agent can run this itself. A new account starts with 100 free credits and no card, which covers dozens of briefings.


### 2. Ask what the meeting is for


Before spending anything, get two sentences: what is the meeting, and what are you selling them. A discovery call and a renewal need different pages. Without the answer the briefing turns into a company profile.


### 3. Search Google for what they have announced


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   execute   \
--action   '{"kind":"connector","integrationSlug":"serper","actionSlug":"search"}'   \
--data   '{"query":"\"Acme\" announces OR launches OR partners","limit":10}'   \
--wait-until-finished


```


` serper.search` takes a` query` and optional` country` ,` locale` and` limit` . The results come back under` organic` , as Google ranks them.


### 4. Read their own pages


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   execute-batch   \
--action   '{"kind":"connector","integrationSlug":"firecrawl","actionSlug":"scrape"}'   \
--records   '[{"url":"https://acme.com"},{"url":"https://acme.com/customers"},{"url":"https://acme.com/careers"}]'   \
--wait-until-finished


```


` firecrawl.scrape` returns each page as` markdown` by default, with navigation, headers and footers stripped. Set` "includeFullPage": true` to keep them, or` "formats": \["links"\]` to list every link on the page. One record is one page.


### 5. Search the news, with a date floor


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   execute   \
--action   '{"kind":"connector","integrationSlug":"exa","actionSlug":"search"}'   \
--data   '{"query":"Acme priorities, challenges and competitors","category":"news","startPublishedDate":"2026-04-16","numResults":10}'   \
--wait-until-finished


```


` exa.search` returns ranked` results` .` startPublishedDate` keeps last year’s news out of this week’s briefing, and` includeText: true` adds each page’s text.


### 6. Read what they are hiring for


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   execute   \
--action   '{"kind":"connector","integrationSlug":"theirStack","actionSlug":"searchJobs"}'   \
--data   '{"companyFields":{"company_domain_or":["acme.com"]},"fields":{"posted_at_max_age_days":90},"limit":10}'   \
--wait-until-finished


```


Open roles are the most under-used input in account research. A company hiring six data engineers is telling you where its budget went, in public and dated. The domain goes in` companyFields.company_domain_or` , not in a record: without that filter the search is not scoped to the account.


For the size, industry and headcount baseline, add` linkedin.enrichCompanyFromDomain` with` {"domain":"acme.com"}` .


## What it costs#


From each action’s credit definition:


Action Credits


` serper.search` 0.05 per search


` firecrawl.scrape` 0.05 per page


` exa.search` 0.175 per search (10 results included), 0.025 per extra result


` theirStack.searchJobs` 0.5 per job posting returned


` linkedin.enrichCompanyFromDomain` 0.5


One briefing with one search, three pages, ten news results and the baseline is about 1 credit, plus 0.5 per job posting returned.` limit` caps the job search, so` limit: 10` caps it at 5 credits.


## Write the briefing#


Keep it to one page, and keep three kinds of line apart:


- **Sourced** : it came back from one of the calls above. Say which.
- **Inferred** : you reasoned it from what came back. Prefix it` Likely:` and say what it rests on.
- **Unknown** : say so. “No public statement on this” is usable in a call. A confident sentence an agent made up is not, because someone will repeat it to the customer.


Close with three questions to ask, drawn from what you found. For a renewal, drop the news search and keep the baseline and the open roles: the account team knows the story, they want what changed.
